title: terminar, -ido, subject pronouns: yo, tú, usted, nosotros, ellos

cards.title: terminar = to finish
cards.body: 'Terminate' is the link; in everyday English, 'finish'.

cards.title: Where little words go: the precise rule
cards.body: Not 'beginning or end'. Little words go after a complete 'to' form or before the changed verb. In he terminado both verbs are changed, so there's only one place: before he.

cards.title: -er / -ir → -ido
cards.body: Both -er and -ir verbs take -ido; there's no '-edo'. Bienvenido = well-come.

cards.title: nosotros / nosotras = we
cards.body: Nosotras for an all-female group. Say s, not z.

cards.title: él / ella: he / she vs him / her
cards.body: Decide first: is it she (ella) or her (la)?

cards.title: tú vs te
cards.body: Tú is 'you' as the one doing the action, in the group with yo, él, ella. Te is 'you' as the one receiving it, with me, lo, la. English uses 'you' for both, but notice he/him and she/her.

cards.title: The object set: me, te, lo, la, los, las, nos
cards.body: Lo covers him, masculine it, formal you, and neutral 'it' (a situation). Change o → a for feminine, add -s for plural.

cards.title: usted = you (formal)
cards.body: From vuestra merced, 'your grace'. Word order is flexible for usted, but the little words still go before the changed verb.

examples.es: Usted lo ve. / Lo ve usted.

cards.title: ellos / ellas = they
cards.body: Ll is 'y' in most places; Buenos Aires and Montevideo say 'zh', and you may hear a 'j'-like sound in Colombia.

cards.title: Two sets of words
cards.body: Doers: yo, tú, usted, él, ella, nosotros, ellos/ellas. Receivers: me, te, lo, la, nos, los, las.

examples.en: I see · you see · he sees · they see · we see
examples.es: yo veo · tú ves · él ve · ellos ven · nosotros vemos
